News.title: Biological attack
News.content:
Key facts

Biological weapons use microorganisms like virus, bacteria or fungi to spread disease

Agents such as anthrax, botulinum toxin and plague could pose a huge public health threat, killing large numbers of people

A biological attack could be confused with a natural outbreak of disease, hampering the response and control

There are fears that pathogens could be modified to become deadlier or more transmissible

Overview

Biological weapons spread infectious agents or toxins to kill humans, animals or plants or contaminate a country’s food and/or water supply. They can be deadly and highly dangerous and spread beyond a country’s borders, making them difficult to control.

While infectious agents have long been used in wartime there are concerns that scientific advances – such as CRISPR gene editing tools and gain-of-function research – could be used by malign actors to modify pathogens to make them even more deadly and transmissible.

The toxin or infectious agent needs to be “weaponised” to be delivered to the target population. According to the United Nations previous bio-weapons programmes have seen the construction of missiles, bombs and hand grenades as a dirty bomb delivery method. Spray tanks have also been designed for vehicles and there have even been efforts to contaminate clothing.

While there are concerns about what could happen if terror groups get hold of bioweapons, many security experts believe that producing them requires a level of sophistication only available to national governments and state-sponsored groups.

Perhaps their greatest power lies in the power they hold in the collective imagination – in a letter to the BMJ in 2001 in the wake of anthrax attacks in the United States psychiatrists from the UK, US and Australia said the (understandable) panic the weapons evoke could cause more harm than the actual weapons themselves.

“The purpose of these weapons is to wreak destruction via psychological means – by inducing fear, confusion and uncertainty in everyday life,” they wrote.

Prevention

The United Nations Biological Weapons Convention came into force in 1975 and it forbids states from developing, producing, stockpiling, or sharing biological agents, toxins and equipment that have no justification for peaceful or defence purposes.

Some 184 countries have fully signed up to the treaty – however, in 2024 the United States government State Department raised concerns about the compliance of China, Iran, Russia and North Korea, all of which are full signatories.

Under the treaty countries can lodge a complaint with the UN Security Council if they believe other member states are violating the convention. The Security Council can investigate complaints, but this power has never been invoked.

History

The use of biological weapons is as old as warfare itself with reports of armies poisoning wells as far back as 600 BC. During the siege of Caffa (a town in modern-day Ukraine) in the 14th century the attacking Tartar forces experienced an outbreak of plague and threw the bodies of their dead comrades over the walls of the town to spread the disease. In 1797 Napoleon flooded the plains around the Italian town of Mantua to start a malaria epidemic.

During the First World War the Germans denied shipping cattle infected with anthrax to the United States and other countries, although its use of chemical weapons in the form of mustard gas is well documented. This led to the first international chemical and biological weapons treaty in 1925. However, during the Second World War many countries, including Britain, conducted bioweapon experiments.

Eventually a bioweapons treaty was signed in 1975, although western governments believe the Soviet Union continued a research programme for many years. In 1979 reports emerged of an anthrax outbreak in Sverdlovsk, near a military facility. The official version of events was that people had died after eating infected meat, however in 1992 the Russian president, Boris Yeltsin, admitted that the outbreak was caused by an accidental release of anthrax spores from a bioweapons facility.

In the 1990s the Aum Shinrikyo cult attacked the Tokyo subway with sarin gas, killing 13 people. Before this they had made three unsuccessful attempts at attacks with anthrax and botulinum toxin. Members had also tried to get hold of Ebola virus.

In 2001 – a week after the 9/11 terrorist attack – letters containing anthrax spores were sent to media organisations and two senators, killing five people. After a long investigation a scientist at the US government biodefence lab in Fort Detrick, Maryland, became the prime suspect but he committed suicide before he could be charged.

News.title: Rotavirus
News.content:
Key facts

Rotavirus is a common infection that causes diarrhoea and vomiting, especially in babies and young children

The rotavirus vaccine is the best way to protect against rotavirus disease

Rotavirus is an RNA virus that is shed in the faeces of infected people

Symptoms of rotavirus include watery diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, and stomach pain

Overview

Rotavirus is a highly contagious virus that commonly causes severe watery diarrhoea and vomiting, particularly in infants and young children. Although most children recover within a few days, some may experience severe dehydration requiring hospital treatment. In very rare cases, rotavirus can be life-threatening. Globally, rotaviruses are the leading cause of severe diarrhoea in young children although the number of deaths has dropped since a vaccine became available.

Signs and symptoms

Symptoms of rotavirus typically begin up to three days after exposure and usually clear up within a week. However, symptoms can last up to two to three weeks.

The most common symptoms include:

Severe watery diarrhoea

Vomiting

Fever

Stomach pain

Additional symptoms can include loss of appetite and dehydration, which can be particularly dangerous for very young children. Signs of dehydration include decreased urination, dry mouth and throat, dizziness when standing, crying with few or no tears, and unusual sleepiness.

Dangers and complications

Rotavirus can lead to significant health risks, particularly due to the potential for severe dehydration, which dangerous for young children. Severe dehydration is treated with intravenous fluids. In some instances, if treatment is delayed, it can result in death. In poorer countries around 2.5 per cent of children who present to health facilities will die.

If a young child has had diarrhoea for more than 24 hours or their faeces is black and/or has blood in it you should take them to a doctor immediately.

Transmission

Rotavirus is primarily transmitted through contact with the faeces of infected individuals. The virus can easily spread in families, hospitals, and childcare centres. Transmission occurs when virus particles enter the mouth via unwashed hands, by touching contaminated objects or surfaces, or by eating contaminated food. People are most contagious when they have symptoms and during the first three days after recovery. They can also spread the virus before they develop symptoms. Rotavirus infections often follow a seasonal pattern, peaking in the winter and spring in countries with temperate climates.

Rotavirus is prevalent globally and, unlike bacterial diarrhoea, it is not linked to poor sanitation and hygiene. It is thought every child will have had it by their fifth birthday.

Treatment

There is no specific medicine to treat rotavirus infection, but your doctor may recommend medicine to treat the symptoms. Antibiotics are not effective against viruses such as rotavirus. The main treatment focuses on managing symptoms and preventing dehydration through oral rehydration therapy, which involves drinking a beverage containing water, sugar, and electrolytes. If dehydration is severe, hospitalisation for intravenous fluids may be required.

Prevention

The most effective way to prevent rotavirus disease is through vaccination. The rotavirus vaccine is part of routine immunisation programmes. In the UK, babies receive two doses of the vaccine at 8 and 12 weeks old. Additionally, practising good hygiene, such as frequent handwashing, is important in reducing the spread of the virus, alongside keeping children and young babies away from school and nursery when they are sick. While the vaccine doesn’t provide complete protection from infection, vaccinated children are less likely to become seriously unwell.

There is also a very small risk – one in 20,000 to one in 100,000 – of a serious problem where the bowel becomes blocked (intussusception) in the week after being vaccinated.

History

Rotavirus was first discovered in 1973 by an Australian team led by Ruth Bishop, who identified the wheel-shaped virus from intestinal biopsies of children with gastroenteritis. By 1980, rotavirus was recognised as the most common cause of severe gastroenteritis in infants and young children in the United States. In the prevaccine era, the was responsible for up to 500,000 deaths among children annually worldwide.

In 1998 the first rotavirus vaccine, RotaShield,was licenced in the United States but was withdrawn over the risk of blocked bowel. In 2005 two new vaccines were introduced and, alongside two additional vaccines, they are now used in more than 100 countries worldwide. Together they have contributed to marked decreases in hospitalisations and deaths from diarrhoea.

The rotavirus vaccine was introduced into the routine UK vaccination schedule in 2013. A study in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2016 found that the number of young children being admitted to hospital for acute gastroenteritis fell by 26 per cent the year after the introduction of the vaccine.

News.title: Polio
News.content:
Key facts

Polio is a serious infection caused by a virus.

It mainly affects children under 5 years of age.

The virus can cause paralysis, and in severe cases, death.

Polio is transmitted mainly through the faecal-oral route.

Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent polio.

Overview

Polio is caused by a virus that invades the nervous system and can cause paralysis within hours. There are three types of wild poliovirus with only type 1 still circulating. Although polio is now only endemic in Afghanistan and Pakistan, the potential threat from its continued circulation means that the World Health Organization (WHO) still classifies it as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

The Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) was launched in 1988, bringing together governments, donors, and health workers to raise awareness of the disease and improve access to polio vaccines. This has led to a 99 per cent reduction in polio cases, and an estimated 20 million children have been prevented from contracting polio since the GPEI was launched.

Signs and symptoms

Most people who contract polio do not have any symptoms. Some individuals develop mild, flu-like symptoms.

High temperature

Extreme tiredness (fatigue)

Headaches

Vomiting

Stiff neck

Muscle pain

These symptoms typically last up to 10 days. In rare cases, polio can lead to more serious symptoms affecting the brain and nerves, including muscle weakness and paralysis, typically in the legs.

Dangers and complications

Polio can lead to long-term or lifelong difficulties. If the paralysis affects the muscles used for breathing, it can be life-threatening. Some patients ended up in iron lungs – coffin like contraptions which helped them breathe. Some individuals may be left with permanent paralysis or other disabilities.

Complications can include:

Muscle weakness

Problems with joints

Swallowing difficulties (dysphagia)

Some people who have had polio may develop symptoms again or their symptoms may worsen, sometimes decades later, which is known as post-polio syndrome. This can cause muscle weakness that deteriorates over time, leading to pain and fatigue, and possibly disability.

Transmission

Polio is a highly infectious disease caused by a virus that spreads easily from person to person. It usually spreads through contact with the faeces of an infected person. This can happen by not washing hands properly and then putting them in the mouth, or through contaminated food or water. The virus multiplies in the intestine. It can also spread through coughs and sneezes, though this is less common. Polio is more common in areas where there is poor access to clean water and sanitation.

Treatment

There is no specific treatment for polio and care is supportive including:

Bed rest in hospital

Painkillers

Help with breathing

Regular stretches and exercises to prevent muscle and joint problems

Specialist help such as physiotherapy or surgery may be required if long-term problems arise from polio.

Prevention

The best way to prevent polio is through vaccination. The polio vaccine is part of the routine childhood vaccination schedule. In the UK, the polio vaccine is given to children at eight, 12, and 16 weeks old as part of the 6-in-1 vaccine, at 3 years, 4 months as part of the 4-in-1 pre-school booster, and at 14 years old as part of the teenage booster.

In addition to routine vaccinations, a polio booster may be required before travelling to certain countries. It’s essential to seek advice from a travel clinic, GP, nurse, or pharmacist before travelling abroad.

Washing hands with soap and water or using hand sanitiser regularly throughout the day also helps to avoid catching and spreading viruses.

History

Polio is an ancient disease, with evidence of sufferers depicted in ancient Egyptian engravings. The first clinical description of the disease was produced by British physician Michael Underwood in 1789. In 1840, Dr Jacob Von Heine, a German orthopaedic doctor, determined that poliomyelitis was a distinct disease and theorised that it had an infectious cause. The poliovirus that causes the disease was identified in 1909 by Austrian immunologist Karl Landsteiner.

Polio vaccines were introduced as routine immunisations in the 1970s, and the number of cases dropped dramatically. But by the late 1980s, polio was still paralysing over 1,000 children a day around the world. Since the launch of the GPEI in 1988 wild poliovirus cases have decreased by over 99 per cent. Type 2 wild poliovirus was declared eradicated in 2015, and type 3 was declared eradicated in October 2019. Type 1 remains in Afghanistan and Pakistan. The discovery of poliovirus in sewers in London demonstrated that the disease could still be a threat – the virus was thought to have been shed by someone visiting and endemic country and there were no active cases of the disease.

Sports.title: Man Utd legend’s daughter stuns in skimpy negligee for sultry snaps as fans say ‘hot hot hot’

THE DAUGHTER of Paul Scholes has sent fans into meltdown with her latest social media post.

The glamorous snap saw her pose in a skimpy negligee as she struck a series of steamy poses.

Sports.title: Former England star reveals Pep Guardiola subbed him off in TRAINING as team-mates left shellshocked
Sports.content:
FORMER Manchester City goalkeeper Scott Carson has revealed Pep Guardiola once subbed him off in TRAINING.

Ex-England stopper Carson joined City as a back-up option in 2019 but only played two games for the club.





He spent six years at the Etihad and was initially third choice to Ederson and Claudio Bravo.

Carson’s main job was to help the senior keepers and prepare the team in training.

But during one session early in his stint at City, he left boss Guardiola unimpressed.

Carson told The Good, The Bad & The Football Podcast about an unfortunate incident during an intra-club friendly.



He said: “The team that was starting on the Saturday, were pressing the goal kick. I think it was a month that I’ve been in there.

“I went in to do this goal kick. He’s stood right there and I’m thinking, ‘Oh my god’. I’m s***ting myself.

“And then he’s like ‘drive it to the half-way line onto their chests there’. I’m thinking, ‘Oh s***.’ I’ve kicked the first one and it just went – I haven’t drilled it. It just went safe.

“And he went, ‘just drill it’. And I’m like, ‘Oh for f***’s sake’. So I’ve done it again but I think I’ve either come off it or it went that way.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I just remember him shaking his head and then he shouted to the goalkeeping coach [Xabier Manscidor]: “Xabi! Where’s Claudio (Bravo)?!

“Basically, he’s subbed me off in training. He’s subbed me and I’m walking off and I think it was John Stones who was looking at me.

“I went, ‘John, I’ve just been subbed in training!'”

Co-hosts Nicky Butt, Paul Scholes and Paddy McGuinness were left in stitches after hearing Carson’s story.



Carson, who is now 40, retired from football last summer after his City contract expired.

He raked in around £8.5m during his stint, averaging £2.8m per save and £354,000 per touch. Carson also won four league titles and the Champions League.

His career lasted more than 20 years after starting at Leeds before playing for Liverpool and West Brom.

He also had spells with Turkish side Bursaspor, Wigan and Derby before his time at City.

Sports.title: What Man Utd ace Benjamin Sesko has learnt from Casemiro and how Bruno Fernandes helped the striker from day one
Sports.content:
BENJAMIN SESKO believes his Manchester United teammates would be “stupid” not to learn as much as possible from Casemiro before he leaves in the summer.

Sesko’s smart finish followed Casemiro’s ninth goal of the campaign during United’s 2-1 win over Brentford at Old Trafford.





The Stretford End chanted “One more year, one year Casemiro” for the departing midfielder, who has just four games remaining after United opted against triggering his contract extension.

Casemiro, 34, has become an inspiration for any player fighting to win back their place in the team after two difficult years.

And 22-year-old striker Sesko said: “You are stupid if you don’t look at him and try to be like him when it comes to the work rate.

“He’s a working machine. He’s experienced, what he’s putting on the pitch is unbelievable.



“You need someone like this. Unfortunately, he’s leaving, but we are pleased that we can manage him until the last minute in the game and we’re going to use him.”

Just over 14 months ago, Casemiro was frozen out of the starting XI for three months and nearly shipped off to Saudi Arabia in January 2024.

Yet, true to the pedigree of a man with five Champions League titles to his name, the Real Madrid legend dusted himself off and fought relentlessly to win Ruben Amorim’s favour.

Casemiro’s leadership and professionalism has rubbed off on certain members of United’s squad. He has started 31 out of a possible 32 Premier League games this season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Sesko added: “The way you look at him, it’s very important, you know? Everyone is pleased that he is here.

“Unfortunately, he leaves at the end of the season, but it’s important to keep him up like this.”

Casemiro ran over 20 yards to embrace Amad on the halfway line after the Ivorian winger made the vital interception that started the breakaway for Sesko’s goal. Amad had endured a poor first half before that.

Casemiro’s celebrations and love for the game have not gone unnoticed.



United’s want to free up space on the wage bill is understandable, as Casemiro earns over £350,000 per week but continues to struggle with the physical demands of the midfield.

Ineos were clear that they would not repeat past mistakes with keeping players for too long.

I’ve looked up to him a lot since I arrived here and he’s helping me a lot.” Sesko on Fernandes

Casemiro’s form will attract European interest, but Saudi and MLS clubs are also swooping in—with a US move looking plausible given his frequent family trips to Florida over the last four years.

The Red Devils are set to sign two new marquee midfielders in the summer transfer window, with Elliot Anderson at the top of their wishlist.

Sesko also wants Carrick to become United’s next permanent boss in the summer.



He said: “He’s an amazing coach, I’ve said this many times. He’s brought different energy.

“Also the way we’re doing in the training, it’s unbelievable and I would like to have him here.”

United are on the verge of Champions League qualification, moving 11 points clear of sixth-place Brighton to cement their hold on third before hosting Liverpool on Sunday.

Sesko said: “[Achieving] the goal that we [had] the start of the season, even though it was difficult to get to this point after what we’ve been through.



“We’re in a good place. We have to keep it up like this. We’re looking forward to the next game, to try and secure the Champions League.”

Sesko’s nine goals in his last 14 games have capped off a debut campaign when he has directly earnt United 14 of their 61 points.

Sesko has scored six goals in 28 Champions League appearances for Leipzig and Red Bull Salzburg, having played in Europe’s elite competition three more times than Bruno Fernandes.

Fernandes set up Sesko’s goal for his 19th assist of the season, meaning he needs two more across the final four games to break Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne’s record.

Sesko said: “He is capable of anything. I’m listening to him on and off the pitch. I’ve looked up to him a lot since I arrived here and he’s helping me a lot.”

On scoring his 11th of the campaign to top United’s goalscoring charts, Sesko said: “Scoring here will never get old.”

The striker said his goal for the season was to “get used to the league” and that he has achieved that by “getting better from game to game”.

Sports.title: Man Utd annoyed at Barcelona’s attempts to lowball them over Marcus Rashford transfer ahead of huge summer window
Sports.content:
FRICTION is growing between Manchester United and Barcelona amid discussions over a knockdown price for Marcus Rashford.

Barca have a £26million option to make Rashford’s season-long loan permanent but there are doubts over whether they will keep the England international.





A third party is continuing discussions on behalf of Rashford, 28, and United sources have expressed irritation at Barca’s attempts to lowball them in negotiations.

Rashford has two years left on his United deal but he is not involved in the club’s plans for the future.

The Red Devils academy graduate has notched 21 goal contributions in the Champions League and LaLiga this season.

But he has not been a nailed-on starter under Hansi Flick, with roughly half of his appearances coming off the bench.

United have scheduled meetings this week to discuss outgoings in the summer transfer window.

Andre Onana, Joshua Zirkzee and Manuel Ugarte will all be free to find new clubs.

Back-up goalkeeper Altay Bayindir is expected to join Besiktas while United could cash in on academy midfielder Toby Collyer.

Casemiro, Jadon Sancho and Tyrell Malacia will all be released.

Micky van de Ven is also being discussed as an option to bolster the defence.

Sports.title: Bournemouth slap £80MILLION price tag on Chelsea and Liverpool transfer target after contract talks stall
Sports.content:
BOURNEMOUTH will demand a fee in the region of £80million for clubs chasing teen sensation Eli Junior Kroupi, SunSports has been told.

The French wonderkid is attracting serious interest from Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City, while sides in France have also held talks with his agent in a bid to lure him back.





SunSport revealed in February that Bournemouth were keen to tie Kroupi down to a new deal to protect their asset and reflect his rising status, but talks have since stalled.

The 19-year-old joined Andoni Iraola’s side last summer after a stunning campaign in France, where he netted 22 league goals to fire Lorient to Ligue 1 promotion.

And he has taken to the Premier League like a duck to water.

Kroupi has already smashed in 11 league goals, becoming the first teenager in two decades to hit double figures in their debut Premier League season.



The last to do it was Republic of Ireland legend Robbie Keane, who scored 12 in the 1999/2000 campaign.

Liverpool icon Robbie Fowler also managed 12 in 1993/94. Kroupi now needs just two more goals from his remaining games to surpass both and stand alone.

His impact has been so big that Bournemouth have barely missed Antoine Semenyo, who joined Manchester City in a club-record £62.5m deal in January.

Club sources have told SunSport that Kroupi will command a fee even higher than that, despite only arriving last summer and still being tied to a long-term contract.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Sources close to the player say he is eager to test himself at the very top level and would welcome a big move this summer, with changes expected at the club both on and off the pitch.

To underline his importance, Kroupi is currently Bournemouth’s top scorer with 11 goals as Iraola’s side push for European football.

In more transfer news- Bournemouth believe they have struck gold again with the signing of highly-rated youngster Ade Solanke from Lorient.

The 18-year-old left-back is currently featuring for the club’s Under-21s but has already been earmarked for a first-team role next season.



The Cherries initially tried to sign Solanke from Irish side Shamrock Rovers when he was just 16, but were blocked by post-Brexit rules.

Instead, sister club Lorient completed the deal, as transfers within the EU were still permitted at that age.

But as soon as Solanke turned 18, Bournemouth swooped to bring him to the South Coast.



He has since impressed for the Under-21s and has already trained with the senior squad.

The club believe incoming boss Marco will continue his development when he replaces Andoni Iraola this summer.

Sports.title: Gary Neville spots ‘cheeky’ Michael Carrick copied controversial Ruben Amorim tactic to help Man Utd beat Brentford
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE called Michael Carrick “cheeky” for reverting to Ruben Amorim’s back three system.

Manchester United beat Brentford 2-1 at Old Trafford on Monday night.





Carrick, 44, initially lined his team up in a 4-2-3-1 formation.

The Red Devils led 2-0 at the break via goals by Casemiro and Benjamin Sesko.

But at half-time Carrick decided to make a change in order to solidify his side.

Noussair Mazraoui replaced Amad Diallo, slotting into a back three alongside Ayden Heaven and Harry Maguire, with Diogo Dalot at right wing-back and Luke Shaw on the left.



Leny Yoro later replaced injured Shaw, with Mazraoui then moving to wing-back.

The tactical tweak limited Brentford’s attacking output, with the Bees having looked a lot more dangerous in the opening 45.

Mathias Jensen scored a brilliant goal on 87 minutes but United managed to hold on.

Discussing Carrick’s tweak on his post-match Sky Sports podcast, Neville said: “It was a really pragmatic safe way.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We’ve won the game already, Brentford look quite dangerous and they’re creating a lot of chances going forward so we need to nullify that and to be fair they did that in the second-half.

“Little bit cheeky going to Ruben Amorim‘s system, the 5-2-3, but these players have played that a lot this season and they know it and I think the extra player at the back paid off.

“Man Utd didn’t concede because of the extra player, it was more the midfield didn’t quite get to Jensen.

“I think the Man Utd fans understood what he was doing in the second-half, they understood that their team were winning 2-0 but it could easily have been 2-2.”



Carrick has revitalised United since replacing Amorim in January.

The Red Devils have virtually secured a place in next season’s Champions League, sitting 11 points above sixth place with four games remaining.

Since returning to Old Trafford Carrick has primarily utilised a 4-2-3-1 formation.

But last night’s match showed that he can be tactically flexible, as he aims to secure the job long-term.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford, Casemiro and Andre Onana lead Man Utd to 'set up two new transfer rules'
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford, Casemiro and Andre Onana lead Man Utd to 'set up two new transfer rules'

Manchester United are planning to avoid Marcus Rashford, Casemiro and Andre Onana transfer repeats in this summer's window

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford and Casemiro decisions have caused Manchester United to have a financial re-think (Image: (Photo by Gareth Copley/Getty Images))

Manchester United are aiming to avoid overspending on signings or becoming embroiled in lengthy negotiations during this summer's transfer window. Sizeable contracts agreed for Marcus Rashford, Casemiro and Andre Onana have been highlighted as one reason for the change in transfer strategy.

‌



United's Monday night victory over Brentford has seen Champions League qualification for next season get closer to being secured and it will undoubtedly help attract high-profile players. Nottingham Forest star Elliot Anderson is a firm target, though Manchester City are also keen on the 23 year old.

‌



£100million has been mooted as his asking price, but should that rise to somewhere in the region of £120million, United will walk away from the deal, with every player having a set price ceiling, according to BBC Sport. Their report further states that United are set to approach this summer's transfer window in a markedly different fashion to previous ones, which includes steering clear of 'getting drawn into protracted negotiations'.

‌



While Casemiro has proved to be an outstanding signing for United, he was not actually a target in 2022. United had spent the majority of the summer chasing Frenkie de Jong, and that deal collapsing meant a substantial sum was committed to the Casemiro transfer in order to push it through.

Michael Carrick told to learn from 'huge' Sir Alex Ferguson trait if he gets Man Utd job READ MORE :

David de Gea shows true feelings towards Man Utd after reuniting with former teammate READ MORE :

Substantial contracts were also handed to Rashford and Andre Onana, which has made it considerably more difficult for the club to move on from both. This has been underlined by fresh reports from Sky Sports Germany suggesting Barcelona are pushing to secure a second loan for Rashford rather than triggering the £30million purchase option.

United appear to have already addressed the Rashford and Onana situations, with Senne Lammens stepping in as United's new No.1 following the latter's loan departure. Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo were also brought in during the summer, with the pair serving as the blueprint for quality signings attracted to the club at sensible fees.

‌



Midfield has now emerged as the most pressing priority, with Casemiro - who netted his ninth Premier League goal of the campaign against Brentford - set to depart at the end of the season, leaving United even more stretched in that area. Anderson remains United's primary target, though Old Trafford chiefs believe there are plenty of viable alternatives available.

View 2 Images Elliot Anderson and Adam Wharton are both transfer targets for Manchester United

‌



Brighton's Carlos Baleba, Crystal Palace star Adam Wharton and Real Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni have all been linked, while Newcastle United's Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes are also on the radar.

Ultimately, United are seeking a long-term midfield partner for Kobbie Mainoo, who has delivered a string of outstanding displays since Michael Carrick's arrival.

Speaking following the victory over Brentford, he said: "Like against Chelsea, he showed he was complete with and without the ball, in both defensive and offensive duties. We know he's capable of it and it's good to see him demonstrate it. He's in great form right now."

Article continues below

Mainoo has also expressed warm praise for Carrick, with the United interim head coach proving instrumental in his return to the England squad. He said: "I've loved every minute of it, especially under the boss now. Just feeling the confidence."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick told to learn from 'huge' Sir Alex Ferguson trait if he gets Man Utd job
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick told to learn from 'huge' Sir Alex Ferguson trait if he gets Man Utd job

Michael Carrick has guided Manchester United to nine wins in 13 games since becoming their interim manager, but they'll be back in Europe next season with more fixtures to juggle

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is in pole position to become Manchester United's permanent manager (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Steve Bruce played 417 games for Manchester United, all of them for his managerial mentor, Sir Alex Ferguson. He was the first man to lift the Premier League trophy after captaining United in the inaugural 1992-93 season.

‌



And after hanging up his boots, he began a 27-year career in management that saw him take charge of 1,094 games at a dozen clubs. He reckons that with the possible exception of an international job, his own life in the dugout is over but hopes that another former United player will be the one whose managerial prowess returns the Red Devils to the top of the tree.

‌



“I sincerely hope Michael Carrick gets the Manchester United job,” said Bruce during an appearance on The Overlap and Betfair’s Stick to Cricket show. “He’s certainly put himself in pole position. He gets the club because he’s been there and played for it. So, I hope he does get it permanently next season.”

‌



Carrick ended up with even more United appearances than Bruce, totalling 464 by the time he left in 2018. More than 300 of those came in the seven seasons he had Fergie for a boss and Bruce knows that kind of influence is priceless experience for those players who want a career in coaching.

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

Ex-Man Utd chief takes Old Trafford plan elsewhere after Sir Jim Ratcliffe demand READ MORE :

And he revealed that the winning mentality was the greatest lesson he took from his former boss. “Sir Alex was huge on preparation,” Bruce said. “I think Fergie was the start of rotation, too - 25-30 years ago, he was the first to change the team.

‌



“It was unheard of back then; your team was your team. But it was all meticulous. Now it comes into the big clubs in particular, all over the world with pre-season. He would say, ‘We’re not doing that, we’re not getting on planes to do that’.

“In the end, it took over because there was that much money involved, but he was huge on preparation. That’s a big key. Tactically, but physically especially, pre-season and all the rest of it. His mentality, though, was to win.

“He would say, ‘We’re Man United and we are the best team, and you are the best players, and we’ve got to prove that week in and week out. The rest of the world don’t like us by the way, but we’ve got to make sure we’re at it’. He was meticulous in that respect.”

‌



Should Michael Carrick get the Manchester United job? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick learned from Sir Alex Ferguson over seven years (Image: Getty Images)

Famously, despite all his success with the best team in the country during the 1990s, Bruce never won a full cap for England but he will be cheering on the country this summer, even though he fears burnout, a problem he knows well from his long time in coaching.

‌



“The French are very good again,” Bruce said. “The Spanish, and then you’re never going to rule out one of the South American teams. England must have a chance of winning the World Cup because of the personnel we’ve got.

“I just have this thing about all the lads who play in the Premier League. They’ve played so much football that you just hope they’re fresh enough. They play Saturday, Tuesday, Saturday.

“The public thinks they should be fine, but after the season, they’re exhausted. They’ve played 60 or 70 games, and then you’ve got to get ready for the biggest tournament. But we’ve definitely got a chance with the team we have.”

‌



View 3 Images Steve Bruce has backed Michael Carrick to get the job (Image: JMEnternational/Getty Images)

And as for his own future? “Never say never, but I believe that I’ve had my time in management. I thoroughly enjoyed it, but there comes a time when you have to call it.

“Maybe something like an international job. I had a conversation with Ireland a few years ago, and before Steve McClaren, I had a chat with the Jamaican FA. They went for Steve in the end.”

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd chief takes Old Trafford plan elsewhere after Sir Jim Ratcliffe demand
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd chief takes Old Trafford plan elsewhere after Sir Jim Ratcliffe demand

Manchester United previously had Sir Dave Brailsford as part of their hierarchy and he unveiled big plans to make them champions again - but has since left to deliver on new ambitions

View 2 Images Sir Dave Brailsford (left) was previously a part of the Man Utd hierarchy (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

Sir Dave Brailsford initiated “Mission 21” and “Mission 1” when he was at Manchester United before being moved on - but has continued with that theme in his new role.

‌



Brailsford, known for his success in the cycling world, came onboard at Old Trafford when Ineos took charge of the club's football operations. His close relationship with Sir Jim Ratcliffe saw him employed to raise standards.

‌



Brailsford now holds the title of director of sport for Ineos and looked to inspire a return to Premier League success for the Red Devils - whilst also eyeing a first title for the women's side. As a result his two "Missions" were inspired by the league titles he hoped to win in Manchester.

‌



Ultimately his stint at Old Trafford was short lived and he stepped away from United after only 18 months to focus instead on Ratcliffe’s cycling team. The men's and women's teams are no closer to winning their respective leagues.

Now back in the cycling world Brailsford has initiated “Mission 8” for staff and riders at the Ineos Grenadiers - formerly known as Team Sky - as they seek to win an eighth Tour de France, reports The Times.

Under the Sky and then the Ineos banner, the team won seven Tour de France titles in eight years between 2012 and 2019. The first of those came when Sir Bradley Wiggins secured a historic first win for a British rider. Chris Froome then took on the mantle, marking himself out as the sport's elite individual.

‌



He won four Tours inside five years for the team. That dominance was then taken on by further victories for Geraint Thomas and Egan Bernal. In more recent years Ineos have struggled to be competitive, which in part has owed to the quality of Tadej Pogacar and UAE Team Emirates XRG.

View 2 Images Egan Bernal was the last Tour de France winner for the Ineos outfit - that coming in 2019

Brailsford played an integral role in the overhaul at United when Ratcliffe initially bought a minority stake in the Premier League club. He was a leading figure in the revamp of the Carrington training complex, which has now been fully completed and attracted praise after year's of neglect.

Article continues below

United's hierarchy is now led by football individuals with Omar Berrada, formerly of Manchester City, and Jason Wilcox making key decisions. Their latest remit is to appoint the club's next manager whilst in the background there continues to be talk of how and when United will produce a world leading stadium.

Sports.title: Benjamin Sesko makes Casemiro claim as outgoing star shines again - 'We'd be stupid'
Sports.content:
Benjamin Sesko makes Casemiro claim as outgoing star shines again - 'We'd be stupid'

Casemiro's farewell tour is coming to an end on a high - and Benjamin Sesko admits the Brazilian legend is someone the whole squad can learn from before he goes

View 2 Images Casemiro is going out on a high at Manchester United (Image: AP)

Benjamin Sesko reckons his Manchester United team-mates would be "stupid" not to learn from Casemiro before he departs Old Trafford. Casemiro has found the form of his life in the final weeks of his time at United, before heading to pastures new this summer.

‌



The Brazilian has scored three goals in his last three home league games, including one in United's crucial 2-1 win over Brentford on Monday night.

‌



The midfielder's form has been instrumental in helping United climb to third in the table, to find themselves on the brink of securing Champions League qualification.

‌



Casemiro has been praised for his work rate and attitude. The vast experience of the former Real Madrid superstar has rubbed off on the likes of Kobbie Mainoo and others around him.

Man Utd receive shocking Marcus Rashford offer from Barcelona in transfer twist READ MORE :

Paul Pogba on doping ban, what hurt him most and living for the moment at Monaco READ MORE :

And Sesko has urged his colleagues to make the most of Casemiro - while they still have the chance. Sesko said: "He’s a working machine. He’s experienced, and what he's putting on the pitch is unbelievable.

"You need someone like this. Unfortunately, he's leaving, but yeah, we have to learn, so we are pleased that we can manage him until the last minute in the game - and we're going to use him.

‌



"Of course, you know, the way you look at him, it's very important, you know (to learn from his example). And I think you can be stupid if you don't look at him and try to be like him, when it comes to the work rate and stuff.

"And again, as I said, I think everyone is pleased that he is here. Unfortunately, he leaves (at the end of the season), but yeah, it's important to keep him going like this."

View 2 Images Sesko celebrates his goal against Brentford

‌



Interim manager Michael Carrick now appears to be in pole position to get the job on a permanent basis this summer.

Sesko admits he would love Carrick to be appointed full-time - and reckons United can go on to achieve anything with him in charge. The Slovenian striker added: "Of course, (he'd like him to stay). He's an amazing coach, I’ve said this many times.

"He's brought a different energy. Also the way we're doing things in the training, it's unbelievable and of course, I would like to have him here. The way before the game fans were giving the sound and everything. You know, we were have starting flying.

Article continues below

"That's why we also created so many chances and yeah, it's been amazing and hopefully we will have more moments like this."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel and England's biggest World Cup headache is obvious 50 days from opener
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel and England's biggest World Cup headache is obvious 50 days from opener

England will start their World Cup campaign on June 17, and until then Thomas Tuchel will sweat on the fitness of key players, as other nations already feel the effects of football's saturated schedule

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel can't ignore other countries' problems (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

Fifty days from today will see England play their World Cup opener with Croatia. And the biggest headache for Thomas Tuchel is injuries, fatigue and withdrawals from the England squad due to fly to the United States.

‌



Football is in serious danger of eating itself with the sheer number of games, the pressure on players and outright greed. Players are being pushed to their limits and we will soon end up killing the golden goose.

‌



This is not just England but a concern for top nations like Spain who are sweating on the fitness of the world’s most exciting teenager in Lamine Yamal. Real Madrid star Rodrygo is a major doubt for Brazil and there are countless other stars like Xavi Simons who will miss the tournament.

‌



The one common theme is too many games, too many demands and a 12-month football calendar. Chelsea star Cole Palmer was left “shattered” after the Club World Cup according to Professional Footballers’ Association chief executive Maheta Molango.

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

OPINION John Cross England Player Ratings: Where are the goals coming from to help Harry Kane?

‌



England icon Sir Geoff Hurst still working aged 84 after several different careers READ MORE :

Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice could be heading for a 70-game season. Other England players like Reece James and Bukayo Saka have been nursing issues all season.

Why on earth would anyone want to serve up a tournament as prestigious as the World Cup with players ending up having to walk around the pitch in searing temperatures and difficult climates? We want fast, exciting football played with skill and intensity. Not walking football. If we are not careful that is what it could become unless players somehow get to recharge.

The World Cup should be the best of the best. It will be a fantastic tournament. Make no mistake about that. Despite everything, it will be a great show. But we also want the stars of the show to be in great shape.

‌



Will England win the World Cup? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 3 Images Xavi Simons has been ruled out of the World Cup with an ACL injury (Image: Andrew Kearns - CameraSport via Getty Images)

We are putting too much on the players and one day - maybe this summer - we will wake up and realise that we are killing the game. Down the years, England have seen players like Steven Gerrard, Rio Ferdinand and David Beckham miss tournaments.

‌



English football - and specifically the Premier League - is fast, physical and demanding. Some players are running on empty and the games are becoming wars of attrition rather than skill. It is a huge concern for England boss Tuchel who will be acutely aware that the players will fly to the States on the back of a tough season.

They are tired and vulnerable to injury. Players who are fatigued are susceptible to muscle injuries. But medics also believe tired players are more likely to suffer serious injuries like ACLs.

This is a massive worry for England because will they really do themselves justice? Look at someone like Morgan Rogers who was a revelation in the autumn and looked as if he would be ready to start for England in the No.10 role.

‌



View 3 Images Morgan Rogers has played 4,427 minutes for club and country this season (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

But Rogers went into the March international break having played more minutes than any other England player and, sure enough, his form has dipped. The World Cup should be the pinnacle of any player and, 50 days out from England’s kick-off, the worry is not whether Tuchel and his players are good enough.

Instead, it’s how many of them will be left still standing? What a sorry state of affairs and worry for the beautiful game.

Sports.title: Arsenal learn PGMOL decision after Mikel Arteta's fury over VAR and Nick Pope incident
Sports.content:
Arsenal learn PGMOL decision after Mikel Arteta's fury over VAR and Nick Pope incident

Premier League referee Jarred Gillett has been appointed to Arsenal's match against Fulham this weekend, just days after Mikel Arteta criticised the decision not to give Nick Pope a red card

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta was not impressed with the decision not to send off Nick Pope (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

Jarred Gillett has been named as the official to oversee Arsenal's fixture against Fulham this weekend, despite provoking Mikel Arteta's fury during the Newcastle match. Gillett was serving as the video assistant referee at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday and opted against intervening when Nick Pope received only a yellow card for fouling Viktor Gyokeres.

‌



Pope raced out of his area to pursue a loose ball but lost his footing and blocked Gyokeres in the 74th minute. Sam Barrott's judgement led him to book the goalkeeper, determining he had not denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, despite Gyokeres appearing to be beyond the last defender.

‌



VAR reviewed and upheld the decision, indicating Malick Thiaw was positioned close enough to have an impact. Gillett was satisfied with Barrott's reading of the incident.

‌



Needless to say, Arteta disagreed with Gillett's judgement. The Spaniard will now have to accept the referee's officiating for an eighth occasion this season.

"In my opinion, it's a clear red card," Arteta said in his post-match press conference. "I've watched it 10 times.

Man City plea to fall on deaf ears as Premier League stick to guns on fixture change READ MORE :

Arsenal transfer target Khvicha Kvaratskhelia performs U-turn on PSG future READ MORE :

"If you have ever played football, it is a red card. It's the second time in two games because I guess [against] Manchester City, when Kai Havertz goes through, [Abdukodir] Khusanov fouls him, 1-1, the title is there, it is a red card, guys. So these are the margins as well and hopefully that's going to change.

‌



"Today, it's a red card; in Manchester and the world, is different; that's it."

Arteta doesn't seem to have garnered much backing for his assessment, though. Ex-Premier League official Dermot Gallagher also felt a yellow card was warranted.

View 2 Images Newcastle goalkeeper Nick Pope fouls Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres (Image: Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

He said: "I thought it was a yellow card. I think he's not moving towards goal, he's not in possession of the ball, he's too far on the wing, and I think there's a covering player.

"There's so many different variations, I think it's possible but not obvious. If you run it again, I don't think Gyokeres would've got the ball because he stops. He anticipates Pope getting the ball, he stops, that's why I think Thiaw will definitely get the ball and not him."

‌



Even ex-Arsenal youngster Jay Bothroyd didn't reckon there was a clear goalscoring chance for Gyokeres. The former Cardiff City forward pointed to the closeness of Newcastle defender Thiaw.

He said: "I agree. There's another angle where you see Gyokeres step on to Pope's boot and that's how he initially goes down. Thiaw is there and is in close proximity to sprint onto that. It's not an obvious goalscoring situation.

"If he gets there, potentially he could, but that's why I don't think it's a red card. Thiaw is close enough where he could probably make a challenge. He's not sluggish, he's quite quick. Pope has impeded him, but he hasn't knocked him over."

Article continues below

Gillett will be joined by assistant referees Simon Long and Steve Meredith, Rob Jones as his fourth official and Peter Bankes as VAR, while the assistant VAR role is taken by Adrian Holmes.

Greaves became the first woman to win a PDC ranking title with a historic 8-7 victory over Michael Smith in Monday's Players Championship 11 final.

The two-time Women's World Matchplay champion took down a trio of former World Champions en route to the title, including Rob Cross, Gary Anderson and Smith in her final three matches of the event.

"I was glued to it," Turner told Sky Sports. "I'm sure she does feel pressure. She's human and she implied in her interview afterwards that she doesn't get to pull those 142 finishes off under pressure, but she doesn't show it.

"We all wax lyrical about how beautiful her throw is, it's so smooth but she uses it to perfection.

"She started to have deeper and deeper runs on the ProTour and there must have been some expectations because she's picked up a record 53 Women's Series titles since the middle of 2022, which is just unbelievable, but it's now transferring it to the next big thing.

"She's won on the Challenge Tour, Development Tour, and now she's won on ProTour, so I can see it happening, but for it to happen so quickly into her first year on the ProTour, that's something really impressive."

A catalyst for more titles

Turner believes her victory on Monday will be a catalyst for winning more ProTour titles, despite Greaves admitting to being in complete shock.

"She's not doubting her ability because you have to put in performance after performance after performance at that level and she has maintained it," Turner said.

"Everyone is super proud of the progress she is making on the oche but she's a great person off it.

"I think there is no ceiling to what she can achieve because she's getting better and her goal now is to take what she's doing on the floor, keep maintaining that, and try and transition that onto the bigger stages."

The sky's the limit for Beau

Image: Greaves has landed a brace of nine-darters in 2026

The World Youth Championship runner-up has made a seamless adaptation to life as a PDC Tour Card Holder, and her latest breakthrough win takes her to within £4,000 of the provisional qualification spots for October's World Grand Prix - live on Sky Sports.

She has also landed a brace of nine-darters in 2026 - the most recent of those coming on the Development Tour on Friday.

"She's shown signs of being able to take her form to the next level on TV," said Turner. "I'm a big believer that when it becomes less scary she will start picking up more wins. How many deeper runs can she have? She's just won a ProTour title. The sky's the limit for her."

'A special, special talent'

Speaking on Sky Sports News, Michael Bridge said: "If she carries on doing well in these ProTour Events she could qualify for some majors but nothing can stop her. The only person is herself because she has said she prefers playing against other women.

"She's absolutely dominated the Women's Series and now that she's won this it could really push her on to win more ProTour titles.

"She's a phenomenal player and I'm really looking forward to seeing how she gets on over the ProTour for the next few years.

"We had Fallon Sherrock winning matches at Alexandra Palace while Lisa Ashton won a Tour Card, but unfortunately during COVID it all had to stop. But we'll be seeing a lot more of Beau Greaves over the next few years. She is such a special, special, talent."

Sports.title: Sinner brushes Norrie aside at Madrid Open
Sports.content:
World No 1 Jannik Sinner recorded a routine 6-2 7-5 victory over British No 1 Cam Norrie to reach the Mutua Madrid Open quarter-finals.

Sinner won a sloppy 35-minute first set in which both players had more unforced errors than winners, breaking Norrie twice to put one foot in the next round.

The second set was a different story for the Brit, though, breaking back and holding serve against the Italian to take a 4-3 lead, but Sinner's quality eventually told, producing a crucial break at 5-5 and holding serve to take the match and secure an impressive round of 16 victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Round of 32 match between Jannik Sinner and Elmer Moller at the Madrid Open

The Wimbledon champion will face the winner of the round of 16 tie between the Czech Vit Kiprova and 19-year-old Madrid native Rafael Jodar in a bid to secure his first Madrid Open title and his ninth at ATP 1000 level.

It's not all bad news for Norrie, though, as he moves back into the world top 20 since 2024.

Image: Norrie is back into the top 20 despite his defeat

"We both knew what to expect [from each other]. I felt like I was serving quite well today through a lot of moments," Sinner said on Sky Sports after the game.

"This surface is very different to other surfaces. It's tough to get the right feedback - sometimes from the outside it looks like you're playing your best, but other times it doesn't feel like you are.

"But I'm happy to be into the quarter-finals - it's a tournament I haven't played a lot, so I'm really happy."

Sports.title: Red Bull deny having best F1 engine, expect upgrade opportunity
Sports.content:
Red Bull boss Laurent Mekies has denied speculation that his team has the best performing power unit in Formula 1 and therefore expects them to be given the chance to improve it during an upcoming engine-upgrade window.

Included in the new power-unit regulations for the 2026 season was a performance-balancing measure - Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) - that will allow those trailing the leading manufacturer by two per cent or more to develop their models.

The first window for upgrades was originally scheduled for after this weekend's Miami Grand Prix but could be pushed back as a result of two of the first six rounds - races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia - having been cancelled due to the conflict in the Middle East.

Despite Mercedes having dominated the opening three rounds of the season to sit top of the standings, 119 points clear of Red Bull in sixth, there had been speculation in the media that the latter actually possess the strongest internal combustion engine (ICE), the power-unit element which is being measured to determine who benefits from ADUO.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Podcast Show, Ant Davidson explains what the recent rule changes are and why we'll see more 'flat-out' racing at the Miami Grand Prix

Mekies told Sky Sports News: "Is it [Red Bull's engine] at the level of the very best? Absolutely not.

"Hence, do we expect to be in that group of people able to be given the possibility to catch up? Yes, we certainly hope to be in that category."

Mekies agreed with Mercedes chief Toto Wolff's recent statement that ADUO should allow manufacturers to "catch up" rather than "leapfrog" rivals, but appears adamant it is the Silver Arrows who have the best ICE.

"I think Toto is right," Mekies added. "The tool is here to catch up, not to leapfrog anyone. So I'm completely with him on that one."

The regulations set out three periods of ADUO during the season, with those adjudged to be at least two per cent behind the manufacturer with the best-performing internal combustion engine awarded development opportunities.

Wolff suggested Honda, who are supplying Aston Martin's engine, are the only manufacturer in need of help from the regulations. The Austrian claimed Red Bull, Ferrari and Audi are in a similar "ballpark" to Mercedes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell weighs in on Max Verstappen's future in Formula 1, admitting he'd 'understand' if the four-time world champion quit

Speaking in a separate interview with the written media, Mekies estimated Mercedes' advantage over Red Bull to be at "three-tenths" of a second per lap, a large amount of which he believes is coming from their ICE.

He said: "What we see is certainly Mercedes, a long way ahead of most of us. And yes, you're right, one guy [Honda] particularly behind.

"The other guys are probably quite close to us, Ferrari and Audi, and fair enough, Honda is probably struggling a bit more.

"To extract the right combustion-engine performance in a fair way across the teams is very difficult. I think overall results are probably giving you the best, the most fair picture, of where everybody is at."

Mekies eyes 'Max effect' after car improvements

Red Bull's poor start to the season has contributed to doubts over whether four-time world champion Max Verstappen will remain with the team beyond the end of the year.

The Dutchman, who says he is unhappy with the 2026 regulations, said in Japan that he is considering stepping away from the sport at the end of the year.

However, Mekies is optimistic upcoming Red Bull upgrades will provide a platform for Verstappen to push forward the car's development, and also lift the Dutchman's spirits.

"The Max we see is a fully committed Max. He wants a fast car and he's helping the team to get a fast car. He's bringing all his energy to that," Mekies said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at Verstappen's disappointing start to the 2026 Formula 1 season

"He's passionate about the sport. As you said, he raised his voice when he felt things needed to be done. We have a step forward for the regulations coming for Miami. He's embracing that. Will it be enough? We have time to see together if it's going to be enough or not.

"We are conscious that the priority is that we give him a car he can push with. And this has not much to do with the regs. We knew we gave him and Isack (Hadjar) a very difficult car in the first three races. And we need to give him a car he can consistently push with.

"Then after, it doesn't mean that it will be fast enough for positions, but it means he can start to bring his 'Max effect' and we can start to build development onto that car.

"And I have every confidence that things may not be fixed for Miami, but that the team is going to get to the bottom of what is limiting us in the same way that they have done last year, and that you will see more and more smile on Max's face."

Sports.content:
"We just started to believe a long time ago, but just couldn't say."

Claudio Braga has told Sky Sports News that Hearts players have been high in Premiership title confidence for much of this dramatic campaign.

The Jambos have led the way for most of the season and are three points clear of current champions Celtic, with Rangers a further point behind.

Braga, who is one of the nominees for PFA Scotland Premiership player of the year, knows the Jambo's first title since 1960 is within their grasp.

"We just wanted to face it game by game and that was really important," the Portuguese forward told Sky Sports News.

Image: Claudio Braga (L) and Lawrence Shankland are nominated for PFA Scotland Premiership player of the year

"Now we know that we are in a place that if we win every game, we win the title. That's something that the city is expecting, the club is expecting and the fans are expecting.

"We need to be calm, and we have a very important game Monday night [vs Rangers], and hopefully we get there with three points.

"We started to believe a long time ago, but just couldn't say nothing like that. Now, just four games to go, it's on us."

The 26-year-old joined Hearts from Norwegian second-tier side Aalesunds last summer and is the club's current top scorer this season with 17 goals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hearts extended their lead in the Premiership title race with victory against Hibernian

"I was thinking is it possible to win silverware, some kind of cup. That was my expectation, and maybe fight for top three.

"That was definitely the expectation when I came to Hearts and tried to fight for my spot.

"I wasn't even sure if I can maybe start or not. The level was different from what I was, so that was a big step for me.

"I wasn't expecting anything that happened this year, so it's just a big surprise, but I'm so glad for it."

Hearts' next Scottish Premiership match is at home to Rangers on May 4, live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: Perrin out, uncapped 18yo included in England Women's T20 World Cup squad
Sports.content:
Davina Perrin has been left out of the England squad announced for the Women's T20 World Cup squad, but uncapped teenager Tilly Corteen-Coleman is included..

Nat Sciver-Brunt will captain the squad on home soil at her seventh T20 World Cup.

She is joined in the squad by uncapped 18-year-old Surrey spinner Corteen-Coleman, Warwickshire's Issy Wong and Durham's Lauren Filer, who are all selected in a T20 World Cup squad for the first time.

Image: Watch the 2026 ICC Women's T20 World Cup live on Sky Sports, with selected games streamed for free via the Sky Sports App

Surrey's Danni Wyatt-Hodge will play in her eighth T20 World Cup.

Somerset's Charlie Dean is the vice-captain and joins a list of impressive all-round cricketers in the squad, with Hampshire fast bowler Lauren Bell set to lead the attack.

England Squad

Alice Capsey, All-Rounder

Head coach Charlotte Edwards said: "There is no doubt that it has been incredibly tough to get to these 15 names. This is the hardest set of selection meetings I have been a part of because the pool of players to choose from is so strong and so many talented players have put their hand up to be a part of the squad, which is exactly what we want. That is the nature of world-class sport, and it is a privilege we don't take lightly to be able to make these difficult decisions.

"An ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 on home soil is a special moment for the game in this country, and we are all really motivated by what could be ahead for this group of players and what they can achieve this summer."

Sciver-Brunt added: "It is a huge honour to be leading England into a T20 World Cup at home in front of family and friends and all our passionate supporters.

"We have all been looking forward to this summer and this tournament for some time now and the naming of the squad means it is almost here and we can't wait to get out onto the field and give it everything to win this World Cup again.

"I know how much winning in 2009 meant to the players and to Charlotte Edwards as captain, and being in the team under Heather Knight's leadership for the 2017 ODI World Cup win was incredibly special.

"Now the aim is to do something similar with this fantastic group of players who I know are putting their heart and soul into achieving our goal, and that hard work will continue right throughout the summer as we start with games against New Zealand and India before that tournament begins."

'Sciver-Brunt and Bell England's players to watch out for'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Michael Atherton says home side England are definitely in the shake up for success

Sky Sports Cricket's Atherton on England's players to watch out for at the Women's T20 World Cup...

"I've got to go with the captain, Nat Sciver-Brunt. It's very important at a home tournament, with a lot of scrutiny, a lot of pressure, a lot of expectation.

"The captain and the leader as a driving force and obviously one of the best players as well, which Nat Sciver-Brunt is.

"Opening bowler Lauren Bell, in English conditions, opening bowling, it's very important to find that movement with the new ball."

England's Women's T20 World Cup record 2009: Winners 2010: Knocked out in group stage 2012: Runners-up 2014: Runners-up 2016: Semi-finals 2018: Runners-up 2020: Semi-finals 2023: Semi-finals 2024: Knocked out in group stage

Image: Heather Knight wants England women to emulate the Lionesses and Red Roses this summer

Heather Knight has told Sky Sports England's ambition at their home Women's T20 World Cup starting in June is to "create a real legacy for women's cricket in this country," emulating the Lionesses and Red Roses.

The 35-year-old says the landscape of women's sport has changed considerably since 2017 and her side's World Cup triumph, with England's Lionesses winning back-to-back Euros titles in 2022 and 2025 - the first in front of a sold-out Wembley - and the Red Roses securing the Rugby World Cup title at a Twickenham full house last September.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Recap the moment England exited the T20 Women's World Cup in 2024 as West Indies were jubilant, while Heather Knight was left in tears

"The focus now is women's cricket at the World Cup so it's really exciting, not too far away now and a chance for us to do something really special as a side," Knight told Sky Sports.

"Home support was huge for us in 2017, the way the crowds built and the final at Lord's, it's super special.

"It's a chance to have a real impact on the sport in your country and leave a legacy. If we do our job right and have success this summer we can leave a real legacy on the sport of women's cricket in this country.

"It took a little bit of time for that success to see changes and I think the landscape is very different now and - particularly in women's cricket - there's the structure beneath the game, the domestic game's professional. It's a lot more normal to be a women's cricketer, there's a lot more visibility.

"You'd hope now if we have that success and things go well for us the structures are in place to make the most of it and really make it a huge moment. We've seen what the Lionesses and Red Roses have done, I've followed those very closely and know some of the players.

"We want to do something similar and hopefully inspire kids to make a girl in cricket really normal and really great."

ODI and IT20 series against New Zealand

In addition to the T20 World Cup squad, the selectors have also named their squads for the Metro Bank One Day series against New Zealand and the two Vitality IT20 series against New Zealand and India that follow.

At the start of a new ODI World Cup cycle, five players are added to the ICC Women's T20 World Cup squad for the three-match Metro Bank ODI series, with first international call-ups for Kira Chathli and Jodi Grewcock.

Sophia Dunkley, Charlie Dean and Danni Wyatt-Hodge will miss the ODI series to manage their workloads, and in the case of Wyatt-Hodge the imminent arrival of her first baby.

Sarah Glenn was not considered for selection due to her continued recovery from a broken finger injury.
